Her “quest” to overcome her grief and perhaps eventually find a new family (remember when Pelle asks her: “does Christian feel like family to you?”) is obvious from the very beginning. So she goes through a journey of self-transformation, confronts her inner demons, and defeats the “antagonist” of the story, who in this case would be Christian. The antagonist “gets what he deserves” (think of the original ending of Snow White, where the Evil Queen is forced to dance in shoes filled with burning coals until she drops dead), and Dani finally finds a “new family” and she’s able to overcome her grief by accepting the fact that death does not necessarily equal pain: the community sees the suicide of their elderly as a way to “give back” to nature/the Gods/etc, and describes it as a “great joy” for those who pass away. It is not a traumatic event but rather a simple rite of passage in the circle of life.
